entries.title: Putin can no longer claim victory in Ukraine, Nobel Peace Prize winner tells BBC
entries.snippet: In an exclusive interview with the BBC’s Steve Rosenberg, Dmitry Muratov says the Kremlin leader can only "destroy Ukraine, not conquer it", with the war now in its fifth year.

entries.title: UK defends seizing shadow fleet tanker after Putin threat
entries.snippet: The UK government says it is "disrupting and deterring shadow fleet vessels" in accordance with the law.

entries.title: More troops to be sent to West Bank village besieged by Israeli settlers

entries.title: Ebola outbreak on track to be deadliest ever, WHO chief says
entries.snippet: The outbreak, declared on 15 May, has caused more than 2,000 deaths, with thousands more reported cases.

entries.title: Travis Kelce shares first details from his wedding to Taylor Swift: 'Best night of my life'

entries.title: Eurovision Song Contest 2027 to be held in Burgas, Bulgaria

entries.title: Zambians voting as president bids for second term

entries.title: Indian actor's video with endangered gibbon sparks investigation

entries.snippet: Grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine are falling as both countries attack each other's shipping facilities and ports.

entries.snippet: Users of the popular streaming platform criticised allowing Amazon to use their data by dafault.

entries.snippet: Inflation cooled a bit last month, according to a new report from the Labor Department. And, ICE plans to equip its officers with electric shock gloves.

entries.title: The drug lenacapavir is a mighty weapon against HIV. Its rollout gets mixed reviews
entries.snippet: It's a twice-a-year injection that is remarkably effective in preventing an HIV infection. Distribution is starting. But questions are being raised about getting it to the areas that need it most.

entries.title: U.S. ambassador calls settler siege of Palestinian homes a 'horrific act of terror'
entries.snippet: The U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee condemned the actions of Jewish settlers who are besieging the home of an American Palestinian family in the Israeli-occupied West Bank.

entries.title: Sailors and their families have lives on pause, uncertain if they'll return to Mideast
entries.snippet: Sailors and family members who were evacuated from U.S. bases in the Middle East months ago are waiting for the military to figure out what will happen to the lives they left behind.

entries.title: These swing voters in Nevada say they are not dismissing socialist candidates
entries.snippet: In online focus groups, 10 of 12 Biden-to-Trump voters said they wouldn't automatically think negatively of a politician who identifies with socialism.

entries.title: New indictment alleges Nick Reiner was lying in wait before killing his parents
entries.snippet: A grand jury has indicted Nick Reiner on murder charges in the killings of his parents, Rob Reiner and Michele Singer Reiner, and adds the allegation that he was lying in wait before attacking them.

entries.title: Millions crowd cities to see Spain's first total solar eclipse in over a century
entries.snippet: As the sky darkened, gradually at first and then quickly, people broke into applause and cheered. It was the Spain's first total solar eclipse in more than a century.

entries.snippet: Three men in Tennessee, Alabama and Oklahoma are scheduled for lethal injection Thursday in a rare convergence of executions on the same day in the U.S.

entries.title: Minnesota man killed his wife and child at daycare after killing another relative, police say
entries.snippet: A Minnesota man killed his wife and their 7-year-old daughter as young children gathered at a home daycare the couple owned before taking his own life, police said Wednesday.

entries.title: Former SPLC official charged in Justice Department's broader criminal case against group
entries.snippet: A former Southern Poverty Law Center official has been charged in the Department of Justice's broader criminal case against the Alabama-based civil rights group, a frequent target of conservative critics who claim the nonprofit is politically biased.

entries.title: Defense in Charlie Kirk's killing argue against death penalty, said shooter hit 'intended target'
entries.snippet: Whether the shooting endangered the crowd is a key issue: Prosecutors cited the risk that other people could have been harmed as an aggravating factor under state law that makes Kirk's killing a capital crime.

entries.title: Karoline Leavitt is leaving her role as Trump's White House press secretary
entries.snippet: Leavitt called it a "bittersweet decision" in a social media post Wednesday shortly after President Donald Trump announced she would be stepping down. She recently returned to the White House podium after the birth of her second child, a daughter named Viviana, in May.

entries.title: Andrew Bird takes eclectic compositions to symphony stages

entries.title: Sam Roberts and Geoff Bennett discuss the art of obituary writing on 'Settle In'
entries.snippet: Journalist Sam Roberts has written some 1,600 obituaries in his decades-long career at The New York Times. His new book, "Are They Dead Yet?" is about the art of obituary writing, how the Times chooses who's worthy of an obit and what that work has taught him about life. Geoff Be

entries.title: Earthquake response strains Colombia's new government and rescuers as they race against the clock
entries.snippet: Tons of aid from regional partners began to roll into Colombia on Wednesday, as the search for survivors in the rubble of powerful earthquake grew more desperate after the temblor razed buildings, buckled roads and crushed cars.

entries.title: WATCH: AG Blanche announces charges over green card scheme involving 'sham' marriages
entries.snippet: The Department of Justice has charged nearly a dozen people with participating in a multimillion-dollar scheme to help hundreds of Chinese nationals fraudulently obtain green cards through sham marriages to U.S. citizens, officials said Wednesday.

entries.title: Bessent said the K-shaped economy 'is over.' Here's what financial experts say
entries.snippet: At a time when many Americans remain stressed about affordability, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has declared that the U.S. economy is no longer in a "K shape," a term used to describe increasing financial inequality between high- and low-income households.

entries.title: Trump's vaccine order hands some MAHA voters a win. It also gives Democrats an attack line
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump pivoted the nation's attention back to vaccines this week with an executive order that aims to scale back the childhood immunization schedule and space out shots into separate visits.

entries.title: 3 states are set to hold executions on the same day, a first in the US since 2010
entries.snippet: Tennessee, Alabama and Oklahoma plan to execute inmates Thursday in what would be the first time in nearly 16 years that three people are put to death on the same day in the United States.

entries.title: PHOTOS: Millions gather to watch Europe's first total solar eclipse in decades
entries.snippet: Millions of people crowded cloudless cities and towns in Spain on Wednesday in search of the best views of a total solar eclipse, when the alignment of the sun, moon and Earth will briefly plunge parts of the planet into darkness.

entries.title: AP report: ICE plans to give its officers gloves that can deliver painful electric shocks
entries.snippet: Immigration and Customs Enforcement plans to spend up to $20 million to purchase thousands of gloves that can deliver painful electric shocks intended to gain compliance from individuals.

entries.title: Inflation cooled last month as gas prices fell, though costs remain elevated
entries.snippet: The modest decline could ease pressure on the Federal Reserve to raise their key interest rate to combat rising costs. Yet prices are still rising more quickly than average wages, underscoring the struggle many Americans have had with more expensive groceries, gas, and healthcare

entries.title: Lindsay Clancy trial turns focus to medications prescribed before she killed her children
entries.snippet: Clancy messaged one of her caregivers less than two months before she killed her three young children in 2023 to say she was having "intrusive thoughts I never had before," "feeling completely hopeless" and worried about becoming addicted to some medications.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: How Germany's drone defense fails
entries.snippet: Drone defense is a priority for the German government. The latest dramatic incident involving an explosive-laden drone at Leipzig airport shows there are still substantial shortcomings.

entries.title: Eritrea: An emerging key player in the geopolitical gamble at the Horn
entries.snippet: Amid growing tensions and security risks at the Horn of Africa, Eritrea, with its strategically important coastal points on the Red Sea and a perceived lack of conflict, is emerging as important player in the region.

entries.title: What would a North Korean surge mean for Ukraine war?
entries.snippet: Ukraine is claiming that North Korea is preparing to send tens of thousands more troops to Russia, where they'll gain valuable battlefield experience. President Zelenskyy has urged South Korea to work closer with Kyiv.

entries.title: Germany: Buildings evacuated over suspected explosive
entries.snippet: Rail traffic was suspended in a region of Bavaria and authorities evacuated buildings around a train station after a suspicious object was found on the tracks. Police later confirmed it did not contain explosives.

entries.title: Germany news: Far-right leader backs left-wing populist
entries.snippet: The leader of the far-right AfD in Thuringia, Björn Höcke, has offered to back populist Sahra Wagenknecht as state premier. And heat-related deaths this year are now numbered at some 12,500. DW has more.

entries.title: India news: Parliament ends turbulent monsoon session
entries.snippet: Prime Minister Narendra Modi was present as the session marked by a fierce standoff over student protests wrapped up. DW has the latest.

entries.title: Colombia earthquake: Rescue operation enters 'final phase'
entries.snippet: Rescuers are racing against a critical 72-hour window to find survivors after a magnitude 7.4 earthquake that has killed 265 people, left hundreds missing, and displaced tens of thousands across western Colombia.

entries.title: US: Karoline Leavitt to step down as Trump's spokesperson
entries.snippet: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt is to leave her job at the end of the month, President Donald Trump says. Leavitt, 28, is the youngest-ever person to have held the position.

entries.title: Does the clean energy transition need forever chemicals?
entries.snippet: As nations globally move to ban forever chemicals, should renewable energy technologies be exempt for the sake of saving the climate?

entries.title: Russia's Putin angers Japan with 1st visit to Kuril Islands
entries.snippet: Japan says it "strongly protests" Russian President Vladimir Putin's trip to the disputed Kuril Islands. Tensions over the Russian-controlled archipelago, claimed partly by Japan, have long dogged bilateral ties.

entries.title: How North Korea has profited from its support for Russia
entries.snippet: Exceptionally high revenues, particularly from war aid for Russia, are consolidating the power of North Korea's autocratic leader. A small number of people in the country are benefiting from an economic boom.

entries.title: Brazil orders Discord to halt livestreaming after teen death
entries.snippet: Brazil has ordered Discord to suspend livestreaming as authorities scrutinize how the platform protects young users. The move follows a case described a "real-life horror show" that has triggered national outrage.

entries.title: Eurovision bars countries at war from hosting
entries.snippet: A Eurovision victory will no longer guarantee hosting rights if war or a wider security crisis affects the winning country. The change could have particular significance for recent high-flyers Ukraine and Israel.

entries.title: Russia: Why is the Yabloko party barred from the elections?
entries.snippet: Russia's supreme court has banned the anti-war opposition party Yabloko from September's parliamentary elections. What does this mean for the election campaign, opponents of the war and for the political mood in Russia?

entries.title: 25 years Ohrid Agreement: Is N. Macedonia's peace holding?
entries.snippet: A quarter of a century after the Ohrid Framework Agreement ended North Macedonia's 2001 conflict, analysts warn that peace between ethnic communities remains fragile.

entries.title: Iran war leaves Iraq running out of money
entries.snippet: Because of the blockage of the Strait of Hormuz, Iraq cannot export enough oil to fund the country's huge public sector. Protests have already started. Will the Iran war destabilize Iraq again?

entries.title: Mozart tribute ends on sour note after mass figurine theft
entries.snippet: A playful tribute to Mozart has turned into a whodunit after 210 gold-colored figures disappeared from one of Austria's busiest tourist spots. The mass theft forced organizers to end the outdoor display early.

entries.title: Unconstitutional? German intelligence to receive more powers
entries.snippet: German intelligence agencies have been calling for more powers in the fight against cyberattacks, terrorism and extremism. Now the government has given the go. Critics warn that red lines are being crossed.

entries.title: Italy: Etna eruption in Sicily halts Catania flights
entries.snippet: Sicily's Catania airport has suspended flights again as Mount Etna continues to spew lava and volcanic ash. The eruption has disrupted travel during the peak summer holiday season.
